statement: For a continuous adapted chordal Loewner driver W with deterministic W(0), dg_t(z)=2/(g_t(z)-W_t)dt, and three deterministic surviving marks W(0)<x1<x2<x3 with positive ordered Xi=g_t(xi)-W_t, if C(X1/X2) and C(X1/X3) are continuous local martingales in the same usual filtration throughout a locally stopped lifetime, then W-W(0) is a continuous local martingale with quadratic variation 6t on that lifetime. Here C is the normalized integral of [s(1-s)]^(-2/3) on [0,u].
assumptions: Usual filtration; W continuous and adapted.
Both specified observables are local martingales in the same filtration.
Localization before denominator degeneracy; conclusion only over the lifetime covered by the premise.
proof_or_counterexample: Invert the first observable to deduce that W is a continuous semimartingale. Quotient Itô gives the quoted equality of signed finite-variation measures for each pair. Subtract the (1,2) and (1,3) identities; their coefficient difference is strictly positive. This forces dV=6dt and dA=0. Complete localized derivation is in ATTEMPT.md.

statement: One Cardy-ratio martingale alone does not identify a Brownian Loewner driver: on 0<=t<1/2, Y=sqrt(4-8t), W=3-3Y/2, g_t(1)=3-Y and g_t(2)=3-Y/2 satisfy the real Loewner equations and C((g_t(1)-W)/(g_t(2)-W))=1/2, while W is nonconstant deterministic finite variation with zero quadratic variation.
assumptions: t<1/2, before either displayed real mark is swallowed.
C is the normalized beta-integral with exponents -2/3.

source.quote: Throughout this interval X/Y=1/2 and C(X/Y)=1/2.

proof_or_counterexample: Y'=-4/Y, so g_t(1)'=4/Y=2/(Y/2) and g_t(2)'=2/Y. The ratio is 1/2. C(1/2)=1/2 by symmetry of its integrand. A third mark x3=3 has ratio derivative -2/27 at t=0, so its Cardy observable is not a martingale under this deterministic driver.
remaining_gap: No gap found by the assigned referee in the explicit deterministic counterexample. It refutes only the general one-observable inference. Different-model gate for store promotion is unestablished.
